The database guardian and continuity guardian both evaluated the trade-off: waiting would cost ~$190,772 in checkout revenue, far exceeding the 60-second business tolerance, while termination required only a 4-minute replay of the idempotent, replayable workload. After an initial termination agreement, the blocker restarted with a new pid, triggering a stale-contract renegotiation before the executor terminated pid 1669575. Verification confirmed full recovery: 100% checkout success over 10s, no active lock waits, and no protected operations aborted. The business has fully recovered within the verification window.

audit.report: During this incident, the batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 1669199 → 1669575) became idle in transaction, holding locks that stalled checkout sessions and reduced success rates, with the business trade-off calculator estimating ~$190,772 in checkout revenue at risk per the 60-second tolerance threshold. The database guardian and continuity guardian both evaluated the trade-off: waiting would cost ~$190,772 in checkout revenue, far exceeding the 60-second business tolerance, while termination required only a 4-minute replay of the idempotent, replayable workload. After an initial termination agreement, the blocker restarted with a new pid, triggering a stale-contract renegotiation before the executor terminated pid 1669575. Verification confirmed full recovery: 100% checkout success over 10s, no active lock waits, and no protected operations aborted. The business has fully recovered within the verification window.
audit.root_cause: The root blocker pid 1669199/1669575 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory) went idle in transaction, holding locks that blocked checkout sessions and caused the ~$190,772 revenue-at-risk that exceeded the 60s business tolerance.
lessons: Pre-documentee the 4-minute replay-from-checkpoint procedure and cost impact for batch_replayable_inventory so that future trade-off calculations can be resolved in a single negotiation round without re-deriving economic impact.

follow_ups: Add a pid-stability guard to the orchestrator: verify the blocker pid matches the current lock-graph root before sealing any recovery contract, and restart observation if the pid has changed.
